clue.text: Give an account of extremely divisive writer

indicators.note: taking a word to its extremes means keeping only its two end letters

blocks.note: the first and last letters of divisive
a scribe is one who writes, a copyist or author

explanation.surface: A reviewer is asked to report on an author who splits opinion sharply.
explanation.definitionFit: To describe something is to set out a spoken or written account of it.

clue.text: Prepare top field

blocks.note: to do a meal or a room is to prepare it
main means chief or top

explanation.surface: A groundsman getting the best pitch ready.
explanation.walkthrough: Field suggests a pitch to prepare, but it means an area of expertise.
explanation.definitionFit: A domain is a sphere of knowledge or activity, the same as a field of study.

clue.text: Another identical stove at home

blocks.note: same means identical
an Aga is a heavy cast-iron range cooker, a British brand
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A householder has bought a second stove just like the first.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aga is a large cooker common in British country kitchens. The answer is what you say at a bar to order a repeat drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordering a repeat round at the bar, 'Same again' and 'Another' are interchangeable requests.

clue.text: Shocking type of music (in key)

blocks.note: rock is a genre of music
taken as written
G is one of the musical keys

explanation.surface: An outrageous style of music, played in a particular key.
explanation.definitionFit: To rock someone is to shake or stun them, so news that is rocking is shocking.

clue.text: Two bouncers about to, very close together

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the paired words go around the short word

blocks.note: a bumper is a bouncer in cricket, a short ball that rears up; two of them
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pair of nightclub doormen poised to act, standing shoulder to shoulder.
explanation.walkthrough: Bouncers suggests nightclub doormen, but in cricket a bouncer or bumper is a ball pitched short to rise at the batter.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic that is bumper-to-bumper has cars packed so tightly that each nearly touches the next.

clue.text: Modest teas prepared after church

indicators.note: tea that is prepared has been made up, so these letters are made up into a new order
after tells us the reworked letters follow the church abbreviation

blocks.note: CH is the standard abbreviation for church
taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: A demure scene of tea being made after the church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste describes someone pure and restrained in behaviour, a synonym of modest in its sense of decent and unassuming.

clue.text: Holds that man's heroin and cannabis

blocks.note: to hold something is to have it
his means belonging to that man
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A drug bust: a man found in possession of heroin and cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: Hashish is a resin made from the cannabis plant, a concentrated form of the drug.

clue.text: Anglo-Irish satirist is fast

blocks.note: first meaning: Jonathan ..., author of Gulliver's Travels
second meaning: quick, speedy

explanation.surface: A literary note that a famous satirist worked quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Jonathan Swift wrote Gulliver's Travels, and his surname is also an adjective for something rapid.

clue.text: An extremely long time — possibly entire year going round Turkey's capital

indicators.note: a capital is a word's head letter, so only the first is kept
possibly suggests one of several arrangements, so these letters may be reordered
going round means encircling, so the reordered letters surround the single letter

blocks.note: taken as written before rearranging
Y is the abbreviation for year
the first letter of Turkey

explanation.surface: A long stretch, maybe a whole year spent travelling around the Turkish capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Turkey's capital suggests Ankara, but here capital means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternity is endless time, and in loose speech any wait that feels interminably long.

clue.text: Vulgar, with what could be no regard for the usual type

indicators.note: what could be invites another arrangement of the letters that follow

blocks.note: common means coarse or vulgar
taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone coarse, and careless of others, typical of the ordinary sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Common-or-garden is an idiom for ordinary or run-of-the-mill, just the usual kind.

clue.text: Impersonate girl in La Bohème beginning to cry

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: Mimì is the seamstress heroine of Puccini's opera La Bohème
the first letter of cry

explanation.surface: An opera singer copying the heroine of La Bohème as she starts to weep.
explanation.definitionFit: To mimic someone is to copy their voice and manner, which is what an impersonator does.

clue.text: Smuggled spirits? Nonsense

blocks.note: first meaning: illicit liquor, smuggled or distilled by night
second meaning: foolish talk or fanciful ideas

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints that the first sense is a mild stretch: the word strictly means illicitly distilled liquor, which was often smuggled too.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both bootleg liquor and empty, fanciful talk, two unrelated senses of one noun.

clue.text: Fancy the Wise Men being taken in in the East

indicators.note: something taken in is enclosed, so one group of letters is placed inside another

blocks.note: the word in taken as written
the Magi are the Wise Men of the Nativity story
E is the abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: The Magi, coming from the East, are taken in as guests.
explanation.walkthrough: The two consecutive ins do different jobs: the first completes the indicator, the second is the outer piece of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy, as a verb, is to suppose or picture something in the mind, a synonym of imagine.

clue.text: Fluid on items, slightly wet

definitions.note: read as the verb phrase 'wet slightly'

indicators.note: something fluid flows and changes shape, so these letters are not fixed in their order

blocks.note: the seven letters of on items, taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: Liquid spilt on some objects has left them damp.
explanation.definitionFit: To moisten is to dampen, making something a little wet rather than soaking it.

clue.text: Clearly guilty, so dismissed during dramatic scene?

blocks.note: in cricket a batter is dismissed when caught
in means during, as in 'in the night'
an act is a section of a play

explanation.surface: A cricketer dismissed in a theatrical moment, as if guilty in public view.
explanation.walkthrough: Caught is a cricket dismissal: the ball is taken by a fielder before it bounces. The question mark admits an act is a division of a play rather than strictly a scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone caught in the act is discovered doing the wrong deed, so their guilt is beyond doubt.

clue.text: Reptile flying at gorilla

indicators.note: letters sent flying are scattered and land in a new order

blocks.note: the nine letters of at gorilla taken as written

explanation.surface: A reptile launches itself at an ape in a jungle fight.
explanation.definitionFit: An alligator is a large crocodilian reptile of America and China.

clue.text: Written outline, showing no care, is sloppy

indicators.note: sloppy work is messy and disordered, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the eight letters of no care is taken as written

explanation.surface: A careless draft plot is criticised as slapdash.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is a written sketch of a plot or a projected sequence of events.

clue.text: See Edinburgh-born inventor in plant

blocks.note: a see is a bishop's diocese, and Canterbury is the most famous English one
Alexander Graham Bell, credited with the telephone, was born in Edinburgh

explanation.surface: An instruction to go and look at a Scottish inventor inside a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: See looks like a verb ordering you to look, but it is the noun for a bishop's seat; plant also suggests a factory before its botanical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The Canterbury bell is a garden flower, a bellflower species with large blue or white blooms.

clue.text: Almost too soon, party married for a title

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: something too soon comes early
a do is a party
M is the abbreviation for married

explanation.surface: A hasty wedding party seems to be angling for a noble rank.
explanation.definitionFit: An earldom is the rank or title held by an earl, a peer of the British nobility.

clue.text: Hold up one who's taking flight across Sweden

indicators.note: lying across something means spanning it, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: a bolter is someone or something that bolts, or runs away
S is the international vehicle code for Sweden

explanation.surface: Stopping a fugitive flying across Sweden.
explanation.walkthrough: Hold up suggests a robbery or a delay, but here it means support.
explanation.definitionFit: To bolster is to prop up or support, which is to hold up something weak.

clue.text: End of August 'orrible? Scorching

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: the last letter of August
the dropped h stands for horrid with its h gone, as a Cockney might say it

explanation.surface: A grumble about a horribly hot August.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'orrible shows a dropped h, so it calls for a synonym (horrid) with the h dropped likewise.
explanation.definitionFit: Torrid weather is intensely hot and dry, the same as scorching.

clue.text: Patent medicine — not rums, unfortunately!

indicators.note: things that go unfortunately go wrong, so these letters end up in the wrong order

blocks.note: the seven letters of not rums taken as written

explanation.surface: A disappointed drinker is handed a quack remedy instead of rum.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostrum is a quack remedy, a patent medicine sold with exaggerated claims.

clue.text: Avoid rear-end of cart or crash

indicators.note: the rear end of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: to shun is to avoid
the last letter of cart

explanation.surface: A driver trying not to go into the back of a cart.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a shunt is informal for a minor car collision, especially one car running into the back of another.
explanation.definitionFit: A shunt is a minor crash, typically one vehicle hitting another from behind.

clue.text: Scored at a brisk speed, a fifty by member run out

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
a leg is a limb, or member, of the body
RO is the scorecard abbreviation for run out in cricket

explanation.surface: A cricket report: a batter makes fifty, then is run out by a fielder.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket scene makes 'Scored' read as making runs, but it means written in a musical score.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegro is the musical direction for a lively, fast tempo, so music marked with it is scored to be played briskly.

clue.text: Supporter of Parliament's lively leader

blocks.note: round can mean brisk or vigorous, as in a round pace
a head is a leader, as of a school

explanation.surface: Praise for the energetic chief of a parliamentary party.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay rather than marking possession. Roundheads were the Parliamentarians in the English Civil War, named for their cropped hair.
explanation.definitionFit: In the English Civil War the Roundheads fought for Parliament against the Royalist Cavaliers.

clue.text: Coach tour rearranged following onset of tonsillitis

indicators.note: the onset of something is its start, so only the first letter is kept
rearranged says the letters are put into another order
following places the reworked letters after the single opening letter

blocks.note: the first letter of tonsillitis
taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: A coach trip is reorganised after someone comes down with a sore throat.
explanation.walkthrough: Coach suggests the bus a tour travels in, but it is the verb or noun for teaching.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutor teaches and trains a pupil privately, which is the sense of a coach.

clue.text: Sharp, boy wearing one

indicators.note: whatever is worn surrounds the wearer, so one word goes around the other

blocks.note: Tim is a boy's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A smartly dressed boy wearing a single item looks sharp.
explanation.walkthrough: Sharp looks like a description of the boy's appearance, but it is the sense in 'six o'clock sharp'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp after a time means exactly punctual, the same as arriving neither early nor late.

clue.text: Find out about unusual sort of photography

indicators.note: out as in out of order, so these letters are disarranged
about means around, so the reworked letters surround the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written before rearranging
rare means uncommon or unusual

explanation.surface: Someone seeks information on an exotic photographic technique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Find out' reads as one phrasal verb, but the two words split into fodder and anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Infrared photography records light just beyond the red end of the visible spectrum, a specialised type of picture-taking.
